# Filing a roadmap

A roadmap is a JSON file the factory loop drives step by step. The driver
validates it with `factory.problems` and refuses anything that does not fit;
the `roadmap-valid` gate runs the same validator on every `*roadmap*.json` you
write, so a bad shape is refused at the Write rather than after lanes and
commits. Check by hand with:

```
python3 $ROOT/.harness/dispatch.py plan validate <file>
```

## The shape

Copy this and fill it in. Every key shown on a step is REQUIRED except
`notes`, `phase`, `scope`, `requires`, `lands`, `ships_off`, `turns_on`,
`blocked_on`, `escalation`, `decided`, `evidence` —
and `lands` is required on a step whose `scope` names more than one repo.
The four steps are the two shapes that fan out (below): E-1 lands the
contract, E-2 and E-3 run at once, E-4 deletes the old form.

```json
{
  "id": "example-2026-09",
  "title": "One line naming what this plan lands",
  "intent": "What is true when every step is done, and why it is worth doing. Name the measurement.",
  "execution": "continuous",
  "model": "claude-fable-5-1",
  "effort": "high",
  "budget": {"max_wall_hours": 8, "max_wakeups_without_evidence": 3},
  "out_of_scope": ["What this plan deliberately does not touch, one item per line."],
  "vision": {
    "rows": ["A ledger row this plan moves, spelled as the ledger spells it."],
    "claims": ["V-7"],
    "moves": "What a customer stops paying for, running or tuning when this lands.",
    "unit": "The unit a cited claim lists, the reading today and the reading expected after.",
    "if_none": "When rows is empty: the claim this serves, or plainly that it is tooling for building forge.",
    "forbids_checked": "For each cited claim, one sentence on how this plan stays clear of its forbids line."
  },
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "E-1-the-contract-lands",
      "title": "The new shared type lands beside the old one, read by nobody yet",
      "status": "todo",
      "phase": "contract",
      "scope": ["forge-platform-wire/src/"],
      "requires": [],
      "notes": "Measured cost, cause, mechanism. Everything a fresh session needs that the acceptance list does not say.",
      "acceptance": [
        "A checkable statement: a test that fails before and passes after, a number that moves, a file that exists.",
        "Another one. Vague acceptance produces a vague verdict."
      ],
      "evidence": []
    },
    {
      "id": "E-2-the-runtime-reads-it",
      "title": "The runtime's callers move to the new type",
      "status": "todo",
      "scope": ["forge-runtime/crates/"],
      "requires": ["E-1"],
      "acceptance": ["The runtime's suite passes reading only the new type."],
      "evidence": []
    },
    {
      "id": "E-3-the-cp-reads-it",
      "title": "The control plane's callers move to the new type",
      "status": "todo",
      "scope": ["forge-control-plane/src/"],
      "requires": ["E-1"],
      "acceptance": ["The control plane's suite passes reading only the new type."],
      "evidence": []
    },
    {
      "id": "E-4-the-old-form-goes",
      "title": "The old type is deleted once nothing reads it",
      "status": "todo",
      "scope": ["forge-platform-wire/src/", "forge-runtime/crates/", "forge-control-plane/src/"],
      "requires": ["E-2", "E-3"],
      "lands": ["forge-platform-wire", "forge-runtime", "forge-control-plane"],
      "acceptance": [
        "No consumer names the old type, and every repo's suite passes with the hub on main first."
      ],
      "evidence": []
    }
  ]
}
```

## The rules the validator enforces

- Top level: `id`, `intent`, `steps` are required. `steps` is an array.
- `execution` is `continuous` (the loop drives it, headless by default) or
  `manual` (a document; the loop does nothing). **There is no `inline`,
  `single`, or `interactive`** — running steps inline in one session is a
  note in `intent`, not an execution value.
- `model`, when present, is a non-empty string naming the tier every turn
  runs on (`/forge-model-tiers`).
- `effort`, when present, is one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`
  (the CLI's `--effort` levels), and it applies to every turn of the driver.
  Leave it out to run at the CLI default: the launch line prints "effort ...
  (from CLI default)". `plan start <plan> -- --effort <level>` overrides it
  for one run. It is the ORCHESTRATOR's effort. A delegated agent's effort
  comes from its own frontmatter.
- Every step: `id`, `title`, `status`, `acceptance` are required; `acceptance`
  is a non-empty array of strings. `status` is free text; the loop asks only
  whether it is one of `done`, `landed`, `landed_v0`.
- `blocked_on`, when present, is `null`, `user`, `ci` or `budget`. An edit
  that newly sets `user` must carry `escalation: {class, why}` naming one of
  the classes below; a step already held for a user before the edit is not
  asked (see deciding, below).
- `escalation`, when present, is `{class, why}`: `class` one of the
  escalation classes, `why` a non-empty line.
- `decided`, when present, is an array of `{at, choice, alternative, why,
  rule}`: `at` an ISO date or timestamp, the next three non-empty strings,
  `rule` optional and non-empty.
- `scope`, when present, is a non-empty array of path prefixes.
- `lands` is the order a step's repos reach main in, hubs first: an array
  naming every repo its `scope` names, once each, and no other (RS-1). A
  step whose scope names more than one repo MUST carry it. The repo is the
  first path component, a lane suffix (`forge-lang--py2`) folded onto its
  repo; a root file like `CLAUDE.md` is no repo. A step's work is not done
  until it is on main in every repo it touched, and a step that never said
  which goes first is how conformance-2026-09 needed two catch-up landing
  steps. Like `vision`, a missing `lands` is asked for only until the
  plan's first step is done; a `lands` that is present is always checked.
- `requires`, when present, is an array of step ids, short (`E-1`) or full.
  A step without it waits on EVERY step before it, so a plan that declares
  none runs one step at a time.
- `sequential_because`, top level, when present, is a non-empty string: why
  this plan is a chain (see shaping a plan, below).
- `stack`, on a step or top level (a step's own wins), when present, is
  true or false. A stacked step whose one unmet `requires` parent has passed
  review opens on lanes cut from the parent's, and the conductor rebases and
  re-verifies it onto main when the parent lands (BE-18). One level deep: a
  step stacked on a stacked step waits.
- `ships_off` and `turns_on`, on a step, when present, are switch names
  (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). A step lands on main when it
  finishes (BE-46), so a customer surface it starts must land OFF: the land
  refuses a step that adds a route, an SDK or WIT op, a checker admission
  (a refusal code removed) or skill text unless it declares `ships_off:
  <switch>` and every file adding the surface carries `#[cfg(forge_switch =
  "<switch>")]`, or it declares `turns_on: <switch>` — the one step that
  finishes the surface, removes the gates and requires every step that
  shipped it off. Text surfaces (WIT, a refusal register, skill text)
  cannot be compiled out and land only with the `turns_on` step. Nothing
  sets the cfg: on is the gate removed, so no app.json key, CLI flag or env
  reaches a switch. A step that adds finished surface on its own declares
  `turns_on` alone.
- `evidence`, when present, is an array.
- `drift`, when present, is `{max_unlanded_hours?, max_ahead_commits?}`: a
  number of hours > 0 and an integer >= 1, no other key (DR-1). The loop
  halts, naming each branch, when a done step's branch has been off
  origin/main longer than the first (default 8) or the plan's lane is
  more commits ahead of main than the second (default 40). Leave it out
  for the defaults; set it only with a reason in `intent`.
- `vision` is required until the plan's first step is done: an object with
  `rows` and `claims` (arrays of strings, either may be empty) and the
  non-empty strings `moves`, `unit`, `if_none`, `forbids_checked`. The
  validator checks presence and type; what the block SAYS is the judge's
  business. A plan already part-done is not asked for one at the Write,
  because the driver rewrites its own roadmap at every landed step — it
  meets the judge at its next `plan start` instead. `vision.one_plan`,
  when present, is a non-empty string (see sizing a plan, below).

## Deciding, not holding (D-140)

A driver that meets a choice takes its own recommended option, unless the
choice is one a person must make for the long term. Rory, 2026-10-19: "Many
of the decisions that wait on me I usually go with recommended, unless I
need to ask you if it is the best long-term product/architecture decision."
So a decision is the driver's unless it falls in one of these classes:

<!-- escalation-classes:start (rendered from factory.ESCALATION_CLASSES; test_be28 checks it) -->
- `vision`: a VISION.md claim, ledger row or refusal
- `product-surface`: a new customer-facing surface, knob or dialect feature
- `contract`: a forge-platform-wire type, the WIT ABI, or a D-n decision
- `security`: auth, RLS, key material or the secrets broker
- `money-or-public`: pricing, billing, or anything public-facing
- `irreversible`: a destructive or outward act the standing rules do not authorise
<!-- escalation-classes:end -->

Outside them: take the recommended option, record it on the step, name it
in the step's report, and keep working. Never `blocked_on` for it:

```json
"decided": [{"at": "2026-10-20", "choice": "the option taken",
             "alternative": "the option a person would reverse to",
             "why": "one line", "rule": "standing rule 2026-10-19"}]
```

`dispatch.py decisions` lists every one from the last 7 days beside the open
decisions, so the veto is one read. Inside a class, hold:
`"blocked_on": "user", "escalation": {"class": "contract", "why": "..."}`,
with the recommendation in `blocked_reason`. The `roadmap-valid` gate
refuses a newly set user hold that names no class.

## Where it goes

In a LANE, never a shared main checkout: `<repo>--<branch>/.harness/roadmap-<name>.json`,
committed there, then `plan start <that file>`. The plan of record may live
elsewhere (translation-engine keeps forge-lang's) and be copied in by
`run-plan.sh`; the copy must not drift from the record.

## Before `plan start`: the CEO

A roadmap is interrogated against the vision canon before it starts
(D-105). Load the `ceo` skill, answer its six questions, and write the
answers into the roadmap as a top-level `vision` object: `rows` (ledger
rows moved), `claims` (`V-n` advanced), `moves`, `unit`, `if_none`,
`forbids_checked`. `plan start` runs the plan-start judge on the file and
refuses a plan whose block is missing, cites a claim the canon does not
define, answers in adjectives, or does something a claim forbids. Its
objections and questions print at the refusal; answer them in the block
and start again.

Write the block when you file the roadmap, not when you start it. The
`roadmap-valid` gate asks for it at the Write on any plan whose steps are
all still todo, because the alternative is what happened to the
evangelist plan on 2026-09-13: filed without a block, driven to 16 of 20
steps, and then held at a restart by a requirement nobody could satisfy
without stopping to answer six questions mid-recovery.

## Sizing a plan

A plan of more than 35 steps carries `vision.one_plan`: the one thing that
makes it one plan and not two or three — a cut that would leave main broken
between the halves, one migration that lands whole. The CEO's judge refuses
it at `plan start` without one, or with a reason that would hold for any
plan ("the steps are related"). conformance-2026-09 grew to 107 steps; a
plan that size cannot land as it goes.

## Shaping a plan to fan out

`plan validate` prints every plan's shape: `critical path L of N steps,
widest level W`. L is the longest `requires` chain, and it is the floor on
how many steps-worth of wall-clock the plan takes however many run at once.
When L is over 70% of N on a plan of 6 or more steps it warns and names the
chain. codebases-2026-10 is 10 levels of 12 steps: nothing at filing said
so. Two shapes turn a chain into a fan:

- **Contract first.** One step lands the shared type or wire contract and
  nothing else; every consumer is then its own step requiring only that one,
  and they run at once. A chain whose later steps each read only what the
  first one landed is consumers of one contract, written in the order
  someone thought of them.
- **Expand and contract.** Add the new form beside the old; move callers in
  independent steps, each requiring only the expand step; delete the old form
  in one last step requiring them all. No step in the middle leaves main
  broken, so none of them waits on another.

The warning is advice, never a refusal: some plans are chains, because each
step reads what the one before it measured. Such a plan says so in a
top-level `sequential_because`, and the warning is not printed. A reason
that would hold for any plan ("the steps are related") is not one.

## Sizing a step

A step's brief must say three things: the bounded file set it touches, the
one coherent change it makes, and how its tests derive from the acceptance
list. A step that cannot say all three is two steps.

The opposite failure is commoner, and it is measured. On 2026-10-22 a review of
the twelve tsx-depth plans found 109 steps for about 59 steps' worth of work, a
46% surplus, because every plan was filed from one skeleton (design, contract,
checker, server, client, forge-ui, skill text, e2e, closing census) and a
"5 to 12 steps" target. Measured costs: a step closed done with no lines
(SS-4); a 9-line portal change as its own step (PH-7); a contract step split
from the checker that read it, 7 h of wall time with 200 lines reworked
(IM-2); a closing census re-run two hours after a "baseline" taken after the
feature (PH-8). Every step is a fresh driver session, a verify and a land, so
a needless step costs hours, not minutes.

So a step is a unit of work that needs its own verify and land, not a layer:

- **Do not split by layer.** A contract lands with the first code that reads
  it. Skill text rides with the checker step that makes it true. An e2e or
  oracle spec rides with the server or client step it proves. A forge-ui
  wrapper of a few dozen lines rides with the client step.
- **A step earns its own entry** only for a different repo's substantial
  change, a real ordering constraint (a hub crate first, a migration before
  a refusal), or a measurement a later step reads.
- **No per-plan closing census.** Plans that share a census share one closing
  reading, filed once as its own small plan. A baseline is taken in step 1,
  before the feature, or not at all.
- **A typical dialect feature is 4 to 6 steps:** design and census, held for
  approval; contract plus checker plus skill text; server with its test;
  client with its forge-ui piece and spec; and only where real, a second-repo
  or migration step. Do not give a plan a step-count target; give it the work.
